[01] One copy

Kept once. Read by every agent.

Skills are how work gets done. Knowledge is what is true. Metrics are what words mean. Each is kept once, in Atlas, and every agent retrieves the same copy under the same access rules.

[02] The product

Three layers. Each one on point.

A context layer is only as reliable as its weakest layer, so Atlas is built as three. Pick a layer, then a part, to see it inside the app.

[03] Under the hood

Reliable by default.

The unglamorous parts are what make context trustworthy. They are on in every workspace, for people and agents alike.

How it works
01Access
Agents sign in as a person over OAuth. Search checks access before it ranks, so an agent never sees more than its person.
02Changes
Agent edits arrive as change requests. A person reads the diff and approves it, block by block.
03History
Every save is a version. Compare any two, restore any one. Deleted pages go to a trash you can restore from.
04Audit
Every read and every write, by people and by agents, in one workspace-wide trail.
05Warehouse
BigQuery and Snowflake, read-only. A metric is SQL agreed once, so every agent gives the same number.
06Models
Atlas calls a model only when a workflow you set up runs, with the provider and key you connect.
07Hosting
Run for you by Ensemble Labs on Fly.io in Paris. One workspace per company, invitation-only.

[04] Connect

One endpoint. Any agent.

Point your agent at Atlas and sign in as yourself. It reads what you can read, and its edits come back to your team as change requests.

  1. Your agent opens Atlas in a browser. You sign in and pick a workspace.
  2. You approve access for this agent. It gets its own grant, never your session.
  3. Every call checks your current access. Lose access to a page and so does your agent.
Every client

terminal

claude mcp add --transport http atlas https://app.atlascontext.ai/mcp/

Run /mcp in Claude Code and sign in.

terminal

codex mcp add atlas --url https://app.atlascontext.ai/mcp/
codex mcp login atlas

The login command opens Atlas in your browser.

.cursor/mcp.json

{ "mcpServers": { "atlas": { "url": "https://app.atlascontext.ai/mcp/" } } }

Cursor asks you to sign in the first time it connects.

terminal

code --add-mcp '{"name":"atlas","type":"http","url":"https://app.atlascontext.ai/mcp/"}'

VS Code asks you to sign in the first time an agent uses Atlas.

Settings › Connectors › Add custom connector

https://app.atlascontext.ai/mcp/

Paste the endpoint, then sign in when Claude asks. Works in the Claude app on desktop and on the web.
